name: Agent platform template, from UnderCover's plans
purpose: A standard set of layers for building an agent product. Each layer names the UnderCover plan that built it, so a new project copies the pattern and replaces only what is specific to it.
reference_project: UnderCover (this repo). Every plan path below is relative to its docs/ folder.
how_to_use: Write the new project's SPEC.md: the business, its users, its rules and what an agent may and may not do.
Choose the layers it needs from 'layers'. Keep their order; a layer needs the layers in its 'depends_on'.
Answer 'before_first_edit' for the project, one line each.
For each layer, write a plan of its own, PLAN_<NAME>.md, from the reference plan, with 'replace' filled in for the project.
Build one layer at a time, phase by phase, as in 'every_plan'.

before_first_edit.auth: Who may call each route, tool and command, and where it is checked. Deny by default.
before_first_edit.tenancy: Whose data each call reads or changes, and the query clause that keeps it there.
before_first_edit.isolation: What the agent can reach beyond its own job: hosts, folders, other users' data.
before_first_edit.secrets: Which keys each part touches, the one host each key goes to, and that none is logged or returned.

every_plan: The brief goes in docs/ first; the plan is docs/PLAN_<NAME>.md, reviewed before any code.
A 'Choices for you' section lists the decisions the documents don't make.
Phases in order, each with a 'Done when' checklist and its own commit.
Tests never call a model: a stub model plays a script, and tools hit the real app in process.
The last phase is live checks with a real model, what they spent, and the documents brought up to date.
docs/STATUS.md records what is built and how to run it.

layers.layer: The pilot: a backend, an agent and a dashboard
layers.gives: A working product with the business rules in the backend
patterns: The backend owns every rule, so a mistaken or misled agent still can't break one; the agent can only ask
One direction of calls: the dashboard and the agent call the backend over HTTP; the backend never imports the agent
Every route has an operation id and a one-line docstring, because they become the agent's tool names and descriptions
A human signs off what the rules say needs a human, such as a payment over a limit
replace: The business rule the backend enforces
layers.skip_when: Never: every later layer builds on it

layers.layer: The harness: tools, middleware and instructions
layers.gives: An agent that works a queue and recovers from a crash
patterns: A queue agent with a to-do list, and a claim agent started fresh for each item
Runs recorded in the backend, so work left half done is found and recovered
Documents read by section, and instructions kept as files the backend serves
layers.skip_when: The agent does one thing per request and never works a queue

layers.layer: Durable state: approvals that wait, and work that survives a restart
layers.gives: An agent that can pause for a person for days and carry on after a restart
patterns: The agent as a LangGraph StateGraph written by hand: a model node, a ToolNode, and the loop between them
A sign-off node of its own that calls interrupt(), resumed with Command(resume=...)
PostgresSaver checkpoints, with durability='sync'
Backend operations safe to repeat: the same decision or payment again returns the same result
replace: The graph's nodes after the model decides
layers.skip_when: Nothing ever waits for a person and every run finishes in seconds

layers.gives: Many items worked at once, and a score of how well the agent agrees with people
patterns: A dispatcher graph with one Send per item and max_concurrency N
Rate limits and timeouts retried up to 3 times; then the item is left with an error and the run goes on
Evaluations on labelled sets, worked on copies so the real data is untouched
A scoreboard with accuracy, cost and time; the agent can never read the answer key
One run at a time: a second start gets 409
replace: The labelled sets and what counts as agreeing
layers.skip_when: Items are worked one at a time and no one needs a measure of quality

layers.gives: Signed-in users with their own permissions, and an agent whose configuration improves under review
patterns: Users sign in; the backend checks each token against the provider's published keys (JWKS), with no shared secret
Who may do what is in a table, such as who may sign off over the limit
Settings stored in the database, with a page of their own
The agent's configuration (instructions, model, effort) in versions
An LLM judge grades each explanation
An improver agent proposes a new version; a person approves it; a rule in code keeps it or rolls it back; a spending limit caps each round
layers.skip_when: No users sign in, and the configuration is changed by hand

layers.gives: An agent that proves who it is, and a backend ready for a serverless host
patterns: An API key for the agent, so the backend knows a call came from the agent
A check for instructions hidden in the data the agent reads
The agent's own API: routes only the agent may call, apart from the users' routes
The payment, or other risky act, happens on a person's sign-off, not on the agent's word
The backend made ready for Lambda: a database connection per request, through a pooler
replace: Where hidden instructions could come from
layers.skip_when: Never for a product that goes on the internet

layers.layer: The context layer, memory and the Gateway
layers.gives: Governed documents the agent can cite, memory of each customer, and tools behind a policy
patterns: A context server over MCP that reads governed files and names each answer's file, owner and review date
The agent's tools through an AgentCore Gateway, where a Cedar policy can refuse a call before it reaches the app
A complete decision record: an approval must match a calculation on file
Memory per customer, searched only under that customer
Every step the agent takes shown on the item's page
replace: The governed documents and their owners
layers.skip_when: The agent needs no documents beyond its own data, and nothing must be remembered

layers.layer: The agent on AgentCore Runtime, and sending work back
layers.gives: The agent deployed as a managed app, and people able to send a decision back
patterns: The answer lives in the app, not the request: signed off or sent back is read from the item's record
Every 'only once' is a conditional update of one row, checking the row count
One slot for the agent's work, in a one-row table
Each piece of work registered as an async task before the agent answers, completed in a finally
Nothing at import: the agent gets ready on its first request
Two routes to the agent, local and Runtime, behind one function in the app
layers.skip_when: The agent runs on your own servers

layers.gives: A chat agent that works for a signed-in user, with that user's permissions, and asks before anything risky
patterns: A hand-written StateGraph: remember, model, tools, confirm, save
A confirm node with interrupt() before any risky act, which checks in code that the user may do it
PostgresSaver checkpoints, so a conversation survives restarts and new sessions
The user's sign-in in the graph's context (context_schema, read through ToolRuntime), never in its config
The app owns the conversations, turns and steps tables; the UI reads only the app
The copilot calls the app with the user's sign-in, never the agent's key; the app refuses a request that carries the key
Waiting in code: a tool reads a run every 5 seconds, up to 15 minutes, with no model calls
Figures worked out in code; the app fills the confirmation card from its records
A second AgentCore app beside the agent, one entrypoint, each turn as an async task
Memory per user, saving only the message and the answer

fits_badly.why: The plan polls about once a second while a turn is working

fits_badly.case: No user in the loop, such as batch jobs
Several agents handing work to each other
fits_badly.why: This is one agent with one graph

layers.skip_when: Users never need to ask questions or act through chat

not_in_the_template.why: A second plan for the pilot under docs/PROCESS_EXTENDED.md. It was never built, and no other plan builds on it.
